question: In the context of the Sangam age of South India, the term "Sangam" refers to ______ .

options.text: a royal festival of Tamil kings
a gathering of South Indian traders
an assembly or "meeting together" of Tamil poets

solution:
The correct answer is __**an assembly or "meeting together" of Tamil poets**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The term **Sangam** refers to the gathering or assembly of Tamil poets during the **Sangam Age**, which is a historically significant period in South Indian history.
 
• The Sangam assemblies were held to compile, critique, and refine Tamil literature, showcasing the cultural and literary richness of the Tamil people.
 
• The Sangam Age is believed to span roughly from **300 BCE to 300 CE**, covering the early historic period of Tamilakam.
 
• These assemblies are said to have taken place under the patronage of the Tamil kings, primarily the **Cheras, Cholas, and Pandyas**, who supported poets and scholars.
 
• The Sangam literature includes works on various themes such as **love, war, ethics, and governance**, providing valuable insights into the socio-political and cultural aspects of the era.
